ANSWER (2-4 sentences):

In NLSY79, a respondent classified as more "patient" on the 1989 household-savings-action proxy (= saving in rather than withdrawing/holding no savings) has lower BMI in 1989 by about 0.30 kg/m² per unit shift (95% CI [-0.45,-0.14], p=1.85e-04, n=6,074, cluster-robust SE on Sample ID; standardized beta=-0.056), equivalent to ~12% lower odds of obesity (OR=0.88, 95% CI [0.82,0.94]). The same direction shows up in the forward 1992 BMI (-0.36 kg/m², p=2e-04, n=5,062), is sharper in the unmarried sub-sample where household savings is not diluted by a spouse (-0.45 kg/m², p=0.032, n=487), and survives as same-sign (smaller magnitude) in the BMI_1981 negative control (-0.20 kg/m², p=0.046). This is associational evidence on household-level savings flow, not a causal estimate of individual discount rate, because (i) no experimental time-preference item exists in the subset, (ii) the 1989 savings measure is respondent/spouse-aggregated, and (iii) three OVB sources are unresolvable from this data: no physical-activity/diet/smoking controls, no pregnancy indicator on the 1989/1992 BMI waves, and attrition that retains higher-ability respondents.

Embedded surprise explicitly authorised by the plan to record: weight_* documentation as "kg" is wrong; the columns are in pounds. The empirical lm-coefficient ratio under "kg-pretend" vs "lb-correct" is 2.2046 — exactly the kg/lb conversion — and the only biologically plausible BMI for 14-22 y in 1981 is under the lb reading.
